BETWEEN:-
 ATISHAY JAIN S/O AVDHESH JAIN, AGED ABOUT 27  YEARS, OCCUPATION:

BUSINESS R/O GANDHI WARD D  EORI P.S. DEORI DISTT. SAGAR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI ASHISH TIWARI-ADVOCATE)

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION KESLI DISTRICT SAGAR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY MS. GULABKALI PATEL-GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending to his arrest relating to FIR/Crime No.08/2023 dated 08.01.2023 registered at Police Station Kesli district Sagar for the offence under Sections 420, 406,
409 & 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is being prosecuted for the aforesaid offences registered against him.
It is contended by the counsel that the applicant has been implicated only on the basis of memorandum of co-accused.

It is contended by the counsel that co-accused Smt. Meena Jain has disclosed the name of the present applicant in the memorandum and on the basis of the said memorandum, the applicant has been implicated.

It is also contended by the counsel that Smt. Meena Jain has been enlarged on bail by this Court and therefore, submits that as no overt act is attributed to the present applicant, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the State while opposing the bail application submits that the case has been registered while considering the allegations pertaining to the irregularities in the center i.e Swa Sahayta Samooh and the co-accused Smt. Meena Jain has stated in her memorandum that the entire work of the center was being conducted by the present applicant and co- accused Rahul,
therefore, submits that the present application filed by the applicant deserves to be rejected.

5. Heard rival submission of the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

A perusal of the case diary reflects that there were irregularities as regards the quantity of the commodities in centre and there was violation of the procurement policy, resulting in loss to the public exchequer.
Therefore, while taking into consideration the memorandum of co-accused Meena Jain, at this stage, this Court is not inclined to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
The co-accused Meena Jain was extended the benefit of bail while taking into consideration the fact that she is a married lady having responsibility to maintain minor child.
7. Accordingly, the present application for anticipatory bail stands dismissed.
8. Certified Copy as per rules.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE Astha Atishay Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10419668/
